stem: Nitrogen, $\text{N}_2$, is the most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere and is very unreactive.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Magnesium and lithium both form nitrides with $\text{N}_2$. These compounds both contain the $\text{N}^{3-}$ ion.
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of magnesium with $\text{N}_2$ to form magnesium nitride.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Solid lithium nitride, $\text{Li}_3\text{N}$, reacts with water according to the following equation.

$$\text{Li}_3\text{N(s)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow 3\text{LiOH(aq)} + \text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$$

State **one** observation you would make during this reaction.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: State the industrial importance of ammonia.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
One method of producing $\text{NH}_3$ is by heating ammonium chloride, $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$, with $\text{CaO}$.

$$2\text{NH}_4\text{Cl} + \text{CaO} \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3 + \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Explain why the reaction of $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ with $\text{CaO}$ produces ammonia.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: Three oxides of nitrogen, $\text{NO}$, $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{N}_2\text{O}$, can be formed under different conditions.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
$\text{NO}_2$ can be formed by different chemical reactions.

Write equations for the formation of $\text{NO}_2$ by:

- the reaction of $\text{N}_2$ with $\text{O}_2$
- the thermal decomposition of magnesium nitrate.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
Molecules of $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ can be formed by the reaction between $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$. The bond between the N and O atoms ($\text{N}\rightarrow\text{O}$) is a co-ordinate (dative covalent) bond.

$$2\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{N}\equiv\text{N}\rightarrow\text{O(g)}$$

The enthalpy change of reaction for this reaction is $+82\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Calculate the bond enthalpy, in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, of the $\text{N}\rightarrow\text{O}$ bond.

Use relevant data from the *Data Booklet* to answer this question.
